desc:
Ad split testing and A/B test setup compares two or more versions of an ad, offer or landing page under fair conditions, so you learn what works. Ecom Swift LLC plans, builds and reads the test in your own ad account.

## What is ad split testing?

Ad split testing, also called A/B testing, means showing different versions of one thing to similar groups of people at the same time and measuring which version gets the better result. The thing tested might be a headline, an image, an offer or a landing page. Everything else stays the same, so any difference can be traced to that one change.

Without a test, you rely on opinion. Someone prefers the blue image, someone else prefers the discount. A test settles that argument with evidence from your own buyers, who matter more than anyone in the meeting.

## How testing improves results over time

Each test teaches you something you can reuse. A winning headline style can shape every future ad. A landing page that converts better lifts every campaign that sends traffic to it. Over several rounds, small gains build on each other, and your cost per result tends to fall because you keep the lessons.

Testing also prevents expensive mistakes. A bold change tried on a small share of budget is a cheap experiment. The same change made across a whole account is a gamble. A test lets you try the bold idea safely.

## What a good test setup includes

- One clear question, such as "does a free shipping message beat a discount?"
- A single variable changed between versions.
- Even budget and an even audience split, so neither version has an edge.
- A minimum number of results needed before anyone reads the outcome.
- A fixed start date and a planned end date.
- Tracking that records the right event for each version.
- A note of what you expect, written down before the test begins.
- A plain-language write-up of the winner and how sure we are.
- A suggestion for the next test, so learning continues.
- An optional landing page variant for testing beyond the ad itself.

## How we run a test

We begin by choosing the test with the most to learn, usually the part of your funnel where people drop off. We write the question, create the versions and set up the split inside your ad account using the platform's own testing tools where they fit. We confirm that tracking counts correctly for every version before any money is spent.

When the minimum number of results is reached, we write the outcome. We state the winner, how confident we are, and what the result means in practice. The Basic package covers one planned test with two ad versions and a reading guide. Standard covers up to two tests, including an offer or headline test, with a written result. Premium runs a short program of tests over two weeks, includes a landing page test and finishes with a roadmap and handover call. Extra tests, a landing page variant or a later recheck can be added.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Test one change at a time.
- Decide how many results you need before you begin.
- Run both versions at the same time of day and week.
- Accept a draw as a real answer.
- Keep a log of every test and its result.

**Avoid:**
- Calling a winner after a few clicks.
- Testing five things at once and learning nothing.
- Changing the budget halfway through a test.
- Testing tiny details when the offer itself is weak.
- Ignoring a result that surprises you.

## Who it is for

This service suits a store owner with several ad ideas and no way to choose between them. It suits a business with a landing page that gets clicks but few enquiries. It also suits an advertiser who has hit a plateau and needs fresh ideas that are proven rather than guessed.

## What we need and how to start

Send your website address, your current best-performing ad and any idea you want to test. We need access to your ad account as a partner or team member, and to your website if a landing page is part of the test, never your passwords. Traffic volume decides how long a test takes: small accounts need longer, and we tell you honestly what is realistic before we start. You pay the platform directly for the test budget.
